cases.reason: Before: line 131 renders `_mutation_block(review)` whenever `review.mutation_attempts` is non-empty, so an all-survived run reaches the mutation block, which is the natural place for the conclusion. The block's body is not shown, so this rests on that inference. After: line 131 adds `and review.set_aside_tests`, so a run with attempts but no set-aside tests skips the mutation block entirely and can finish without the non-discrimination conclusion.

BEFORE: line 178 `if unobserved:` routes only runs with unobserved tests to NOT_ATTEMPTED, so a fully completed run with no red test falls through to SURVIVED (lines 187-192). AFTER: line 178 is `if not unobserved:`, so a run where every test completed and none failed now returns NOT_ATTEMPTED, which is the defective behavior; the SURVIVED return is reached only when tests were unobserved.

Before, line 643 passes `mutation_attempts=attempts` into the Review, so survived attempts reach the stored review. After, line 643 passes `mutation_attempts=[]`, so attempts are computed but not wired into the Review the caller sees, which is the defective behaviour.

Before: line 145 uses `outcome.reason or "..."`, so the execution-stage reason is kept whenever one exists and the canned text is only a fallback. After: line 145 always uses the canned string "the test failed against the code as delivered", discarding outcome.reason, so the record can misstate why a non-passing test did not settle.

Before: line 127 `if not self.settled and not has_reason` raises for any unsettled attempt with an empty reason, which is the expected behaviour. After: line 127 only raises when outcome is KILLED and reason is empty, so unsettled outcomes (not killed) with an empty reason are accepted, which is the defective behaviour.

Before: the NOT_ATTEMPTED MutationAttempt gets reason=_why_unobserved(unobserved, result.outcomes), so the runner's reason is stored. After: line 184 is reason="", so the not_attempted attempt is stored with an empty reason and the runner-produced reason is dropped.

BEFORE, line 209 passes `execution=execution` into `run_review`, so the execution configuration (presumably carrying the continue-anyway setting) reaches the pipeline. AFTER, line 209 hardcodes `execution=None`, which drops the whole execution tier rather than just ignoring the flag, so it disables a feature and is not the specific DEFECTIVE behaviour.

Before: _set_aside_block loops over review.set_aside_tests and emits each test's kind, test_id and reason (lines 313-315), so tests are named with reasons. After: the loop is replaced by a single generic count line ("N test(s) were set aside", line 313), so no test is named, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour.

Before: line 479 and line 509 pass `verdicts` to `derive_support`, but the code shown does not reveal whether set-aside tests were already filtered out of `executed_verdicts` or `pair_mapping.verdicts`. After: line 509 explicitly appends `[v for v in pair_mapping.verdicts if v.test_id in set_aside_tests]` to the `derive_support` input, so verdicts from set-aside tests are fed into support and still influence the rating.

BEFORE: line 457 calls _run_execution_tier(...) ahead of judge_pairs, so the execution stage runs before the static judgement. AFTER: that call is replaced by `attempts, executed_verdicts, set_aside_tests = [], [], []`, so the execution functions are never invoked and judge_pairs runs as the effective first stage, which is the defective behaviour.

BEFORE: `_run_execution_tier(...)` (line 457) runs first and `judge_pairs` (line 461) runs afterward on `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)`, which is the expected order. AFTER: line 457 replaces the execution call with empty lists, so execution never runs, and `judge_pairs` still follows and judges all defects. Code-reading is not run before an execution stage, because no execution stage exists. The edit disables the execution tier rather than reordering the stages, so it is not the DEFECTIVE ordering.

Before: judge_pairs receives remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets), so the static judgement runs on defects execution did not settle and its verdicts are recorded in `verdicts`. After: judge_pairs gets the full defect_sets, so static judgement still runs and is recorded, and the execution tier is not gated off or bypassed. The edit instead drops the filtering, so the model re-judges already-executed pairs, a different behaviour from the DEFECTIVE one of returning no static judgement.

Before: `settled` is built only from `attempt.settled`, which names defects execution actually answered, so not_mutable and not_attempted defects stay in the remaining sets sent to static judgement (line 85). After: the comprehension also adds `attempt.outcome is MutationOutcomeKind.NOT_ATTEMPTED` (line 88), so those defects are filtered out of `keep` and dropped from the static judgement, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour for not_attempted.

Before, line 85 removes only defects with `attempt.settled`, so every unsettled defect stays in the returned `DefectSet`s that the static judgement consumes. After, line 85 removes only KILLED defects, which should be a subset of settled, so unsettled defects are still kept in consumable form. The edit may also pass surviving defects to static judgement, but that is a different behaviour from the one named.

Before: the validator at line 151 raises whenever `self.settled and self.descriptor is None`, so every settled attempt must carry a descriptor. After: line 151 adds `and self.outcome is MutationOutcomeKind.KILLED`, so a settled non-killed attempt (e.g. survived) with descriptor None is accepted, which is the defective behaviour. The settled attempt is stored with no injected text to display.

BEFORE: line 288 `if descriptor is not None:` renders the injected text for every attempt with a descriptor, regardless of settled status. AFTER: line 288 becomes `if descriptor is not None and attempt.settled:`, so unsettled (not_mutable/not_attempted) attempts skip the injected text and only print the reason at line 302.

Before: lines 105-111 reject a defect with no regions as not mutable before any execution, which is the expected behaviour. After: that early check is removed, so an empty regions list falls through to _sources and then the `if not readable` check at lines 112-115, which still returns _not_mutable before any execution. The defect with no region is therefore still rejected mechanically, only with a different reason message. The edit does not introduce the defective behaviour of reaching later validity steps or being treated as valid, so it is neither defective nor unchanged.

Before: the only halt is `if baseline.halted: raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` at line 284, and descriptor validity (build_descriptors, from_mapping) is computed separately, so mechanical checks alone settle validity. After: line 284 adds `and not execution.allow_failing_tests`, which only changes when the baseline halt is raised. It does not make execution control flow decide whether a mutation descriptor is valid, so it is not the defective behaviour; it is a different change to halting logic.

Before, `_parser_for` returns the parser for any suffix in `_PARSERS`, so every file type that has a parser is re-parsed after mutation. After, line 140 adds `suffix in {".py", ".pyi", ".json"}`, so only those three suffixes are ever parsed and other parseable types skip the check.

Before: the `if not regions` branch reports 'the defect names no changed region with text at head, so there is no span to replace', which explicitly says no region was named and so there is nothing to edit. After: that branch passes only 'no single contiguous edit was found that would make this defect true', a generic inability message that never says the defect is not editable for lack of a named region.

Before: line 479 merges executed_verdicts (from _run_execution_tier) into verdicts, but the code shown does not reveal whether those verdicts hold executed-line/coverage data or only test outcomes/mutation results, so the defect cannot be judged. After: line 479 drops executed_verdicts from verdicts, so execution results no longer reach derive_support; that removes a data source rather than producing line-coverage-derived support, so it is not the DEFECTIVE behaviour and is not clearly the EXPECTED one either.

Before, the only line span rendered (lines 289-290) is where a defect was injected, and the killing tests are listed as bare IDs (line 295), so no line-execution data is shown. After, line 295 appends ` lines {span}` to every killing test ID, so the report now shows a line span attached to each test, which reads as the lines that test covered.

BEFORE: lines 128-133 only parse when `parse is not None`, so a file with no parser skips the check and falls through to `return None` (valid). AFTER: line 128-129 returns "not mutable because it has no parser" when `parse is None`, so parser absence becomes a rejection instead of a non-issue.

Before: `_parser_for` loops over the hardcoded `_PARSERS` table with `endswith`, so only listed extensions get a parser and any other parseable type is skipped. After: `_PARSERS.get(path[path.rfind("."):])` still looks up only the same hardcoded table, so unlisted parseable types still get no parser. The edit changes how the suffix is matched (for example, `rfind` with no dot returns -1 and slices the last character), but the set of recognized extensions is still fixed, so the defective behavior remains.

Before: lines 127-128 only parse when `parse is not None`, so a file without a parser falls through to `return None` (valid). After: line 128-129 returns 'does not parse: no parser available' when `parse is None`, rejecting the file solely for lacking a parser.

BEFORE, line 129 runs `run_tests(requested, ...)` on the deduplicated list of the named test_ids, so the baseline is limited to the named candidates. AFTER, line 129 runs `run_tests(test_ids, ...)`, which hands the full raw input list to the runner. That is the DEFECTIVE behaviour: the baseline takes the whole test id list and runs it all, with the deduplication dropped. If the caller passes every discovered id, the whole suite runs.

Before: line 138 calls run_tests(tests, root, config), passing only the named candidate tests `tests`, which is the expected behavior. After: line 138 passes list(_sources(regions, root).keys()), the source file paths of the defect's regions rather than the full discovered test list. That is neither the named tests nor the complete suite, so it is a different, likely broken behavior rather than the defective one.

Before: the record has a `tier: EvidenceTier` field (default STATIC) that can be set to DEFECT_KILLED, so executed verdicts can be distinguished from predicted ones. After: only the default changes to DEFECT_KILLED (line 227), so the field still exists and the record shape is not the defective one with no marker; the edit instead makes predicted verdicts default to the executed tier, which is a different problem.

Before, _reason returns past-tense observed text ('The test failed when the defect was injected.', 'still passed when...'). After, lines 109, 111 and 112 return conditional forecasts ('would fail if the defect were injected', 'would still pass if...'), which is the predictive phrasing the defect describes.

BEFORE: _PARSERS includes ".json": json.loads alongside .py and .pyi, so JSON files are parsed after the edit and malformed output is rejected (ValueError is in _PARSE_ERRORS). AFTER: the ".json": json.loads entry is removed, leaving only .py and .pyi, so JSON files are not parsed and can pass validity when broken.

Before: the `except _PARSE_ERRORS as error:` branch at line 132-133 returns a rejection message, so a parse error marks the edit invalid. After: line 132-133 is `except _PARSE_ERRORS: pass`, so execution falls through to `return None` at line 135 and the edit is accepted as valid despite the parse error.

Before, judge_pairs receives remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets), so the code-reading judgement still runs on whatever execution did not settle, including every defect when execution is off. After, the first argument is a hard-coded [], so judge_pairs is called but never judges any defect, and only the execution tier's verdicts reach `verdicts`. This matches the defective behaviour of the delivered path never effectively reaching the code-reading judgement.

BEFORE, judge_pairs receives `remaining_defect_sets(attempts, defect_sets)` (line 465), so defects that execution settled skip the code-reading judgement and only `executed_verdicts` cover them. AFTER, line 465 passes the full `defect_sets`, so every defect still goes through judge_pairs and `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts` keeps that judgement in the output.

The defect concerns a project that cannot be run, but the shown code only handles `baseline.halted`, which in the docstring means a candidate test is already failing, not that the project is unrunnable. Before (line 285) raises ReviewHalted; after (line 285) returns empty attempts and verdicts with set_aside. How `establish_baseline` treats an unrunnable project is not visible, so neither version can be classified for the named behaviour.

Before: the `if unobserved:` branch (lines 178-185) returns `MutationOutcomeKind.NOT_ATTEMPTED` with a reason, so the static judge keeps its conclusion. After: that same branch (lines 178-184) returns `SURVIVED`, so a run execution could not settle is recorded as proven-weak tests, which can replace or alter the static conclusion.

Before, _set_aside_block appended f"  [{test.kind.value}] {test.test_id}" for each set-aside test, so the report named them. After, line 314 drops {test.test_id}, leaving only the kind and reason, so tests are shown as set aside without their ids or names.

Before, line 644 stores `set_aside_tests=set_aside_tests` on the Review, so the failing control-run tests are carried into review state for the report. After, line 644 is `set_aside_tests=[]`, so the computed failing tests are dropped and never reach the review or report, which is the defective behaviour.

Before: line 284 `if baseline.halted: raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` stops the review ahead of `run_mutations` whenever the baseline is halted, which is the defective behaviour. After: line 284 raises only when `baseline.halted and execution.allow_failing_tests`, so a baseline halted by failing tests with the flag off no longer raises and execution reaches `run_mutations` on line 292. `run_mutations` is not shown, so I assume it runs with that baseline rather than skipping.

BEFORE: lines 71-79 return _not_attempted for every defect when `baseline.usable_tests` is empty, so no tests run against the altered copy. AFTER: that guard is removed and the flow reaches the `_attempt` list comprehension (lines 72-83) with `baseline.usable_tests`, so tests are still executed; only the `baseline.halted` short-circuit remains, which is a different condition.

Before, the unobserved branch (lines 179-185) passes `tests_run=tests`, so the candidate tests are still recorded as run against the altered copy. After, line 183 follows `descriptor=descriptor` directly with `reason=...` and `tests_run` is gone, so a partly observed run is recorded as `NOT_ATTEMPTED` with no tests executed, which is the defective behaviour.

BEFORE, line 113 filters regions to those whose path equals descriptor.path, so containment is checked only against regions in the single file the descriptor names. AFTER, line 113 `named = list(regions)` drops the path filter, so a span can be judged contained by a region in a different file; the edit's descriptor path and the region it is credited to can diverge, which is the defective multi-file mismatch.

Before: lines 208-214 build a MutationDescriptor with one path, start_line=result.start_line, end_line=result.end_line and one replacement, so the single span is recorded faithfully. After: line 211 sets end_line=result.start_line, which collapses every span to one line and corrupts the end bound; it is still a single-file, single-span descriptor with explicit bounds, so it does not nest spans or drop/obscure the boundaries, but it changes the span's content, which is a different behaviour than the defect describes.

Before, lines 105-111 return _not_mutable when `regions` is empty, which declines the defect as expected. After, lines 105-108 replace the empty list with a fabricated placeholder Region (path "", lines 1-1) and carry on to _sources, the descriptor builder and the mutation run, so the guard no longer rejects a defect that names no region. I could not see _sources, so a later check might still reject the placeholder, but not with the required 'no single continuous edit' record.

Before: contains() uses `self.start_line <= start_line and end_line <= self.end_line`, which requires both bounds to be inside the region. After: line 36 changes `and` to `or`, so a span is accepted if only one bound is satisfied (e.g. start after region start but end far beyond region end), letting spans outside the named region pass.

BEFORE: lines 130-134 compute invalidity_reason and return _not_mutable when it is not None, so an invalid descriptor is refused before mutated_copy at line 137. AFTER: line 134 is changed to `pass`, so the reason is computed but ignored and mutated_copy/run_tests at lines 137-138 run on an out-of-region or non-contiguous descriptor, which is the defective behaviour.

Before: invalidity_reason checks only mechanical validity (line 96 span exists, line 104 bound, containment, parse), so it accepts any larger non-minimal edit within the bound, which is the DEFECTIVE behaviour. After: line 104 loosens the bound to max_edit_lines + 1, so it still accepts non-minimal edits and accepts even larger ones; the DEFECTIVE behaviour remains.

Before: line 284 `if baseline.halted: raise ReviewHalted(baseline)` stops before mutation whenever the baseline halted. After: line 284 adds `and execution.allow_failing_tests`, so the halt is raised only when failing tests are allowed. When they are not allowed (the case that should halt), it falls through to build_descriptors and run_mutations, which is the defective behaviour.

Before: the verdict sets kills=test_id in killing with tier=DEFECT_KILLED, so each failing test is marked as killing the defect (lines 62-64). After: kills=False and _reason(..., kills=False) are hardcoded, so failing tests in attempt.killing_tests are no longer recorded as killing and the verdict has the wrong kills shape.

BEFORE, line 479 sets `verdicts = executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts`, so executed verdicts from failing tests on mutants enter the recorded list passed to the ledger and `derive_support`. AFTER, line 479 is `verdicts = pair_mapping.verdicts`, so `executed_verdicts` is dropped; the execution tier still produces `attempts` that are only used to filter `remaining_defect_sets`, so the failing-test result stays an attempt and never becomes a recorded discriminating verdict.

Before, Review gets pair_verdicts=verdicts, which the comment says holds both judged and executed provenances. After, line 641 uses pair_mapping.verdicts, the static pair-judgement verdicts (the same object that supplies unjudged_pairs), so executed verdicts are dropped from the review record, which is the defective behaviour.

BEFORE (line 479) simply concatenates `executed_verdicts + pair_mapping.verdicts` and leaves every tier as it was, but the tier given to executed verdicts is set inside `_run_execution_tier`, which is not shown, so I can't say whether they are weaker or already DEFECT_KILLED. AFTER (line 479) leaves `executed_verdicts` untouched and relabels only the static `pair_mapping.verdicts` as `EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED`, so it upgrades a different set of verdicts than the executed ones the defect names.

Before: line 64 sets tier=EvidenceTier.DEFECT_KILLED on the executed verdicts, so they carry the stronger tier, matching the DEFECTIVE behaviour. After: line 64 sets tier=EvidenceTier.STATIC, so the verdicts stay at the weaker tier, matching EXPECTED. Whether render_report() includes the mutation block is not visible here, so only the verdict tier can be judged.
